thought_title: One God, Revealed in His Son

edition.witness_note: Lake 1912 Loeb copy-text; Lightfoot/Funk middle recension not yet locked as second witness

source_text: εἶς θεός ἐστιν, ὁ φανερώσας ἑαυτὸν διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ, ὅς ἐστιν αὐτοῦ λόγος ἁπὸ σιγῆς προελθών, ὃς κατὰ πάντα εὐηρέστησεν τῷ πέμψαντι αὐτόν.
pass_a_gloss: There is one God, who manifested himself through Jesus Christ his Son, who is his Word that came forth from silence, who in all things was well pleasing to him who sent him.
pass_b_english: There is one God. He has made himself known through Jesus Christ, his Son, who is his Word, come forth from silence, and who in every way pleased the One who sent him (John 8:29).

choices.english: his Word, come forth from silence
choices.why: Lake's Greek is positive: the Word proceeds from silence. The negative 'not proceeding from silence' belongs to the interpolated long recension.
rejected: his eternal Word, not proceeding forth from silence

choices.why: God reveals himself through the Son; aorist rendered as completed act.

anf_compare.notes: The English supplied with this excerpt already reads 'his Word proceeding from silence', matching Lake. The old 1885 ANF ('not proceeding forth from silence') follows the long recension and diverges.

bible_refs.note: ὁ πέμψας με ... τὰ ἀρεστὰ αὐτῷ ποιῶ πάντοτε; pleasing the One who sent him

notes: Clause excerpt from Magnesians 8.2 (from εἷς θεός to the end of the chapter); exact substring of the supplied Lake text, preceding ὅτι omitted.
Same English as ignatius_magnesians_8 for this clause.
Source shows 'ἁπό' (for ἀπό); reproduced as supplied.
